skill.name: media-downloader
skill.description: Search, download, and trim image or video assets from stock media sources and YouTube. Supports bilingual prompts, custom output folders, and local media trimming.
skill.summary: Download and trim media assets from stock sources and YouTube.
skill.author: yizhiyanhua-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill performs the advertised media search, download, and trimming workflow, but it uses external services, yt-dlp, ffmpeg, environment API keys, and local file writes. Several static alerts are documentation or placeholder false positives, while user-controlled filenames, unbounded downloads, and broad video download support remain real risks. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Normalize generated filenames, remove path separators, and verify that resolved paths stay inside the selected output directory.

remediation.issue: External media tools process user-controlled URLs and files
remediation.suggestion: Validate accepted URL domains, require explicit user confirmation for downloads, and run yt-dlp and ffmpeg with restricted output paths.

remediation.issue: Downloads do not enforce size or type limits
remediation.suggestion: Check Content-Length and MIME type before writing, enforce a maximum byte limit, and stop streaming when the limit is exceeded.

remediation.issue: API keys are stored in shell profiles and may appear in URL query strings
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a restricted config file or keyring, avoid query-string credentials where possible, and document key rotation steps.

remediation.issue: Default downloads are stored under a hidden skill directory
remediation.suggestion: Use a visible user-selected download directory by default or prompt before storing media under hidden application folders.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Query Text Used In Filenames
semantic_findings.description: Image and video filenames are built from the user search query without removing path separators. A crafted query could write downloaded content outside the intended output folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The filename is derived directly from args.query and joined with output_dir before writing downloaded bytes. The reviewed code does not normalize or constrain the final path.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Streaming Downloads To Disk
semantic_findings.description: The download loops stream response bodies to disk without checking Content-Length, content type, or a maximum byte limit. Large responses can exhaust disk space.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both image and video download functions write chunks until the server finishes. I found no size cap or MIME validation in the reviewed code paths.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Third-Party Video Download Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly supports downloading and extracting audio from YouTube URLs. This can enable copyright or terms-of-service abuse if used without rights checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation advertises YouTube download and audio-only workflows, and the CLI exposes matching options. The code does not include license or authorization checks.

content.value_statement: Finding usable images and clips across different sources takes time. This skill searches stock libraries, downloads selected media, and trims video clips from one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Searches Pexels, Pixabay, and Unsplash for images when API keys are configured.
Searches Pexels and Pixabay for stock video clips.
Downloads YouTube videos or audio through yt-dlp when the tool is installed.
Trims videos by start time, end time, or target duration with ffmpeg.
Saves downloads to a default folder or a user-selected output folder.
Reports configured API keys and required local tools through a status command.
limitations: Most image and stock video sources require user-provided API keys.
Video download and trimming require yt-dlp and ffmpeg on the local system.
The skill does not verify copyright, licensing, or platform terms for downloaded media.
The current implementation does not fully sandbox output paths or download sizes.

use_cases.description: Download several candidate images for a presentation, article, or mockup.

use_cases.title: Prepare Short Video Clips
use_cases.description: Find stock footage and trim it to a requested duration for editing work.

use_cases.title: Build Reference Libraries
use_cases.description: Search multiple media sources and save examples for later review.

prompt_templates.title: Download Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Download five high quality images of modern office desks to my media folder.

prompt_templates.prompt: Find three stock video clips of ocean waves under 20 seconds and save them to my project folder.

prompt_templates.title: Trim a Video Segment
prompt_templates.prompt: Download this YouTube video and keep only the section from 60 seconds to 90 seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Search Before Downloading
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for city night media across image and video sources, then show the best options before downloading.

output_examples.input: Download five sunset photos for a blog header.
output_examples.output: The skill searches configured image sources, downloads matching photos, and reports the saved folder.

output_examples.input: Find a 15 second ocean wave clip.
output_examples.output: The skill searches stock video providers, downloads a suitable clip, and trims it when needed.

output_examples.input: Download only the audio from this video.
output_examples.output: The skill uses yt-dlp to save an audio file when the local dependency is installed.

best_practices: Use a visible, project-specific output folder for each download task.
Confirm media licenses and platform terms before using downloaded assets.
Store API keys securely and rotate them if they may have been exposed.
anti_patterns: Downloading copyrighted videos or audio without permission.
Using broad writable folders as output locations for automated downloads.
Requesting large media batches without size limits or review steps.

faq.question: Does this skill require API keys?
faq.answer: Yes for most image and stock video searches. YouTube download does not require these stock media API keys.

faq.question: Which local tools are needed?
faq.answer: The Python requests package is needed for API downloads. yt-dlp and ffmpeg are needed for video download and trimming.

faq.question: Where are files saved?
faq.answer: Files are saved in the skill downloads folder by default. A custom output folder can be provided.

faq.question: Can it trim videos automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It can trim by start and end time, or reduce a clip to a target duration.

faq.question: Does it check media rights?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify licensing, attribution rules, and platform terms before using downloaded media.

faq.question: Is this safe for unrestricted automation?
faq.answer: No. It uses network access, external commands, and filesystem writes, so review output paths and requested downloads.
